title: The Monkey Gardeners
text:
In the royal park at Benares, a festival was announced, and the king's gardener wanted to go and enjoy it with everyone else. But the young trees in the park needed watering. So he went to the monkeys who lived there and asked their king if his monkeys would water the saplings while he was gone. The monkey king agreed.

When the gardener had left, the monkey king gave his orders. Water was precious, he said, so they must not waste it. Before watering each tree, they should pull it up and look at its roots. Trees with long roots need a lot of water, and trees with short roots need only a little.

The monkeys set to work with great diligence. They pulled up every sapling, examined the roots, gave each one carefully measured water, and planted it again.

A wise man passing through the park saw what they were doing and asked why. When they explained, he remarked that fools who try to do good end up doing harm. The young trees, uprooted one by one, withered and died.
lesson: Following a sensible rule without understanding its purpose can wreck the thing it was meant to protect. Make sure the people carrying out your plan understand what it is for.
people: Monkeys and their king, the king's gardener, the Bodhisatta
